source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Durham campus publishes 40 MW of IT capacity, the largest figure of any data center in North Carolina and about 80 percent of the state's published total.

The campus pairs that 40 MW with 420,000 square feet of technical space, which works out to roughly 95 watts per square foot. That is a conventional hall density, not an extreme one, so the published numbers describe a facility sized for standard enterprise and cloud deployment as much as for dense AI training. Whether the halls are built for the higher rack densities that current accelerators require is not published. The operator lists no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power usage effectiveness.

The state context is what makes the number matter. Five North Carolina facilities publish a megawatt figure, and they total 50.266 MW. Nineteen facilities are mapped in the state, so most publish nothing, and the published total is a floor rather than a census. Under either a 40 kW or a 100 kW per-rack assumption, this is the only campus in the state whose published capacity could host a meaningful training cluster.

What the data does not cover is large. There is no address, no postal code, and no certifications, so nothing can be said about compliance regimes, tenants, or actual power draw beyond the IT figure. The rack counts above are assumptions about density, not claims by CyrusOne. The suitability score of 69 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
